threats.name: Container Base Image Backdooring
threats.description:
When a technical asset is built using container technologies, Base Image Backdooring risks might arise where base images and other layers used contain vulnerable components or backdoors.

See for example: https://techcrunch.com/2018/06/15/tainted-crypto-mining-containers-pulled-from-docker-hub/

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to deeply persist in the target system by executing code in deployed containers.

threats.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
threats.description: When a web application is accessed via web protocols Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) risks might arise.

risk.impactComment: If this risk remains unmitigated, attackers might be able to trick logged-in victim users into unwanted actions within the web application by visiting an attacker controlled web site.

threats.name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
threats.description: For each web application Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) risks might arise. In terms of the overall risk level take other applications running on the same domain into account as well.

risk.impactComment: If this risk remains unmitigated, attackers might be able to access individual victim sessions and steal or modify user data.

attributes.threagile:asvs: V5 - Validation, Sanitization and Encoding Verification Requirements

threats.name: DoS-risky Access Across Trust-Boundary
threats.description: Assets accessed across trust boundaries with critical or mission-critical availability rating are more prone to Denial-of-Service (DoS) risks.

risk.impactComment: If this risk remains unmitigated, attackers might be able to disturb the availability of important parts of the system.

attributes.threagile:asvs: V1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements

threats.name: Excessive Agency
threats.description: An AI agent decides on its own which tools to call and with which arguments. An agent that can change critical systems, directly or through the tools of an MCP server, without a human approving the change, does whatever a prompt injection, a hallucination or a misunderstanding makes it do.
categories: OWASP ASI02:2026 Tool Misuse and Exploitation
OWASP ASI03:2026 Identity and Privilege Abuse

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers who steer the agent, or the agent's own mistakes, might change or delete critical data and trigger actions with real-world effects.

threats.name: Missing Authentication
threats.description: Technical assets (especially multi-tenant systems) should authenticate incoming requests when the asset processes sensitive data.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to access or modify sensitive data in an unauthenticated way.

threats.name: Missing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
threats.description: Technical assets (especially multi-tenant systems) should authenticate incoming requests with multi-factor (MFA) authentication when the asset processes or stores highly sensitive data (in terms of confidentiality, integrity, and availability) and is accessed by humans.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to access or modify highly sensitive data without strong authentication.

threats.name: Missing Build Infrastructure
threats.description: The modeled architecture does not contain a build infrastructure (devops-client, sourcecode-repo, build-pipeline, etc.), which might be the risk of a model missing critical assets (and thus not seeing their risks). If the architecture contains custom-developed parts, the pipeline where code gets developed and built needs to be part of the model.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to exploit risks unseen in this threat model due to critical build infrastructure components missing in the model.

attributes.threagile:asvs: V1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements

threats.name: Missing Cloud Hardening
threats.description: Cloud components should be hardened according to the cloud vendor best practices. This affects their configuration, auditing, and further areas.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might access cloud components in an unintended way.

attributes.threagile:asvs: V1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements

threats.name: Missing Hardening
threats.description: Technical assets with a Relative Attacker Attractiveness (RAA) value of 55 % or higher should be explicitly hardened taking best practices and vendor hardening guides into account.

risk.impactComment: If this risk remains unmitigated, attackers might be able to easier attack high-value targets.

threats.name: Missing Identity Store
threats.description: The modeled architecture does not contain an identity store, which might be the risk of a model missing critical assets (and thus not seeing their risks).

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to exploit risks unseen in this threat model in the identity provider/store that is currently missing in the model.

threats.name: Missing Network Segmentation
threats.description: Highly sensitive assets and/or data stores residing in the same network segment than other lower sensitive assets (like webservers or content management systems etc.) should be better protected by a network segmentation trust-boundary.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers successfully attacking other components of the system might have an easy path towards more valuable targets, as they are not separated by network segmentation.

attributes.threagile:asvs: V1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements

threats.name: Missing Vault (Secret Storage)
threats.description: In order to avoid the risk of secret leakage via config files (when attacked through vulnerabilities being able to read files like Path-Traversal and others), it is best practice to use a separate hardened process with proper authentication, authorization, and audit logging to access config secrets (like credentials, private keys, client certificates, etc.). This component is usually some kind of Vault.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to easier steal config secrets (like credentials, private keys, client certificates, etc.) once a vulnerability to access files is present and exploited.

threats.name: Missing Web Application Firewall (WAF)
threats.description: To have a first line of filtering defense, security architectures with web-services or web-applications should include a WAF in front of them. Even though a WAF is not a replacement for security (all components must be secure even without a WAF) it adds another layer of defense to the overall system by delaying some attacks and having easier attack alerting through it.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to apply standard attack pattern tests at great speed without any filtering.

attributes.threagile:asvs: V1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements

threats.name: Sensitive Data Disclosure through Model Output
threats.description: Whatever a language model or an agent can read, it can be talked into writing: data in its prompt, in its context window, in the documents it retrieves or in its training data. A model that has confidential data at hand and answers callers from the internet, from users or from another trust zone may hand that data to callers who are not allowed to see it.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might extract confidential data, other users' data or the system prompt through crafted questions.

threats.name: Unverified Model Supply Chain
threats.description: Model weights are code in all but name: they decide what the system answers, and some model formats run code when they are loaded. Models that are self-hosted, fine-tuned or pulled from a model registry can be swapped, backdoored or poisoned anywhere between their training and their deployment.
categories: OWASP LLM04:2025 Data and Model Poisoning
OWASP ASI04:2026 Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might deploy a backdoored or tampered model that answers as they want, leaks data or runs code on the systems that load it.

threats.name: Prompt Injection
threats.description: A language model cannot tell the instructions of its prompt apart from the data in it. Content that reaches a model or an agent from users, the internet or another trust zone can carry instructions of its own, either directly in a request or indirectly in a document, a web page or a tool response the model reads, and so take over what the model does.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might make the model leak what it has access to, give misleading answers, or, for an agent, use its tools and permissions for their own goals.

attributes.threagile:asvs: V5 - Validation, Sanitization and Encoding Verification Requirements

threats.name: Publicly Shared Cloud Snapshot
threats.description: Snapshots and images of cloud disks, databases and virtual machines (like EBS or RDS snapshots and EC2 AMIs) can be shared with all accounts of the cloud provider. A snapshot shared publicly by mistake hands everything stored on the asset to anyone.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might restore a publicly shared snapshot or image and read the data stored on it, including credentials baked into an image.

threats.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
threats.description: When a server system (i.e. not a client) is accessing other server systems via typical web protocols Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) or Local-File-Inclusion (LFI) or Remote-File-Inclusion (RFI) risks might arise.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to access sensitive services or files of network-reachable components by modifying outgoing calls of affected components.

attributes.threagile:asvs: V12 - File and Resources Verification Requirements

threats.name: SQL/NoSQL-Injection
threats.description: When a database is accessed via database access protocols SQL/NoSQL-Injection risks might arise. The risk rating depends on the sensitivity technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to modify SQL/NoSQL queries to steal and modify data and eventually further escalate towards a deeper system penetration via code executions.

attributes.threagile:asvs: V5 - Validation, Sanitization and Encoding Verification Requirements

threats.name: Unauthenticated MCP Server
threats.description: An MCP server, or another server exposing tools to AI agents, acts on the systems behind its tools with its own permissions. When it does not authenticate its callers, anyone who can reach it can call those tools, and it cannot tell one agent or user from another to limit what each may do.
categories: OWASP ASI02:2026 Tool Misuse and Exploitation
OWASP ASI03:2026 Identity and Privilege Abuse

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers who reach the server might call its tools directly and read or change what they reach, bypassing the agents and their controls.

threats.name: Unchecked Deployment
threats.description: For each build-pipeline component Unchecked Deployment risks might arise when the build-pipeline does not include established DevSecOps best-practices. DevSecOps best-practices scan as part of CI/CD pipelines for vulnerabilities in source- or byte-code, dependencies, container layers, and dynamically against running test systems. There are several open-source and commercial tools existing in the categories DAST, SAST, and IAST.

risk.impactComment: If this risk remains unmitigated, vulnerabilities in custom-developed software or their dependencies might not be identified during continuous deployment cycles.

threats.name: Unencrypted Technical Assets
threats.description: Due to the confidentiality rating of the technical asset itself and/or the stored data assets this technical asset must be encrypted. The risk rating depends on the sensitivity technical asset itself and of the data assets stored.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to access unencrypted data when successfully compromising sensitive components.

threats.name: Unguarded Access From Internet
threats.description: Internet-exposed assets must be guarded by a protecting service, application, or reverse-proxy.

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to directly attack sensitive systems without any hardening components in-between due to them being directly exposed on the internet.

attributes.threagile:asvs: V1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements

threats.name: Vector Store Poisoning
threats.description: Language models and agents answer and act on what they retrieve from vector stores, for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) or as the memory of an agent. Whoever can write into the store decides what the model believes: a poisoned document or memory entry carries false facts or hidden instructions into every answer that retrieves it, long after it was written.
categories: OWASP LLM04:2025 Data and Model Poisoning
OWASP LLM08:2025 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
OWASP ASI06:2026 Memory and Context Poisoning

risk.impactComment: If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might plant content that misleads the model, injects instructions into its prompts or makes it disclose data, persistently and for every user.

mitigations.name: Container Infrastructure Hardening
mitigations.description: Apply hardening of all container infrastructures (see for example the CIS-Benchmarks for Docker and Kubernetes and the Docker Bench for Security). Use only trusted base images of the original vendors, verify digital signatures and apply image creation best practices. Also consider using Google's Distroless base images or otherwise very small base images. Regularly execute container image scans with tools checking the layers for vulnerable components.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS/CSVS applied?

mitigations.name: CSRF Prevention
mitigations.description: Try to use anti-CSRF tokens ot the double-submit patterns (at least for logged-in requests). When your authentication scheme depends on cookies (like session or token cookies), consider marking them with the same-site flag. When a third-party product is used instead of custom developed software, check if the product applies the proper mitigation and ensure a reasonable patch-level.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: XSS Prevention
mitigations.description: Try to encode all values sent back to the browser and also handle DOM-manipulations in a safe way to avoid DOM-based XSS. When a third-party product is used instead of custom developed software, check if the product applies the proper mitigation and ensure a reasonable patch-level.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Anti-DoS Measures
mitigations.description: Apply anti-DoS techniques like throttling and/or per-client load blocking with quotas. Also for maintenance access routes consider applying a VPN instead of public reachable interfaces. Generally applying redundancy on the targeted technical asset reduces the risk of DoS.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Least Agency
mitigations.description: Give the agent only the tools and the permissions its task needs, read-only where possible, and with the identity of the user it acts for rather than a broad technical one. Require a human approval for changes to critical systems and tag the agent or the link with human-in-the-loop when it is in place. Limit the rate and the scope of actions and log every tool call.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Authentication of Incoming Requests
mitigations.description: Apply an authentication method to the technical asset. To protect highly sensitive data consider the use of multi-factor authentication for human users.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
mitigations.description: Apply an authentication method to the technical asset protecting highly sensitive data via multi-factor authentication for human users.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Build Pipeline Hardening
mitigations.description: Include the build infrastructure in the model.

mitigations.name: Cloud Hardening
mitigations.description:
Apply hardening of all cloud components and services, taking special care to follow the individual risk descriptions (which depend on the cloud provider tags in the model).

For Amazon Web Services (AWS): Follow the CIS Benchmark for Amazon Web Services (see also the automated checks of cloud audit tools like "PacBot", "CloudSploit", "CloudMapper", "ScoutSuite", or "Prowler AWS CIS Benchmark Tool").
For EC2 and other servers running Amazon Linux, follow the CIS Benchmark for Amazon Linux and switch to IMDSv2.
For S3 buckets follow the Security Best Practices for Amazon S3 at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/security-best-practices.html to avoid accidental leakage.
Also take a look at some of these tools: https://github.com/toniblyx/my-arsenal-of-aws-security-tools

For Microsoft Azure: Follow the CIS Benchmark for Microsoft Azure (see also the automated checks of cloud audit tools like "CloudSploit" or "ScoutSuite").

For Google Cloud Platform: Follow the CIS Benchmark for Google Cloud Computing Platform (see also the automated checks of cloud audit tools like "CloudSploit" or "ScoutSuite").

For Oracle Cloud Platform: Follow the hardening best practices (see also the automated checks of cloud audit tools like "CloudSploit").

mitigations.name: System Hardening
mitigations.description: Try to apply all hardening best practices (like CIS benchmarks, OWASP recommendations, vendor recommendations, DevSec Hardening Framework, DBSAT for Oracle databases, and others).

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Identity Store
mitigations.description: Include an identity store in the model if the application has a login.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Network Segmentation
mitigations.description: Apply a network segmentation trust-boundary around the highly sensitive assets and/or data stores.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Vault (Secret Storage)
mitigations.description: Consider using a Vault (Secret Storage) to securely store and access config secrets (like credentials, private keys, client certificates, etc.).

attributes.threagile:check: GetAttribute a Vault (Secret Storage) in place?

mitigations.name: Web Application Firewall (WAF)
mitigations.description: Consider placing a Web Application Firewall (WAF) in front of the web-services and/or web-applications. For cloud environments many cloud providers offer pre-configured WAFs. Even reverse proxies can be enhances by a WAF component via ModSecurity plugins.

attributes.threagile:check: GetAttribute a Web Application Firewall (WAF) in place?

mitigations.name: Output Data Protection
mitigations.description: Give the model only the data the caller may see: filter retrieved documents by the caller's permissions before they reach the prompt, keep secrets and other users' data out of prompts and training data, and filter the output for sensitive data. Do not rely on the system prompt to keep anything secret.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Model Provenance
mitigations.description: Take models only from trusted sources, pin them by digest and verify their signatures or hashes before they are loaded. Keep a bill of materials of the models and their training data (an ML BOM), prefer formats that cannot run code when loaded (like safetensors), restrict who can write to the model registry, and evaluate a model before it reaches production.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Prompt Injection Defenses
mitigations.description: Treat everything a model reads as untrusted, including retrieved documents and tool responses: keep instructions apart from data (for example with clearly delimited and labelled content), filter input and output, and give the model and its tools only the permissions the task needs. Require a human approval for actions with side effects, and monitor for injection attempts. See the OWASP GenAI Security Project at https://genai.owasp.org/.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Snapshot Sharing Restrictions
mitigations.description:
Prevent the public sharing of snapshots and images with a cloud configuration rule that revokes it, and audit the sharing settings regularly. Do not bake credentials into images; see the secrets management cheat sheet at https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html.

For Amazon Web Services (AWS): Turn on block public access for EBS snapshots (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/block-public-access-snapshots.html) and for AMIs (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/block-public-access-to-amis.html) in every region, use the AWS Config managed rules ebs-snapshot-public-restorable-check (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/ebs-snapshot-public-restorable-check.html) and rds-snapshots-public-prohibited (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/rds-snapshots-public-prohibited.html) with an automatic remediation, and review the snapshot findings of IAM Access Analyzer (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/what-is-access-analyzer.html).

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: SSRF Prevention
mitigations.description: Try to avoid constructing the outgoing target URL with caller controllable values. Alternatively use a mapping (whitelist) when accessing outgoing URLs instead of creating them including caller controllable values. When a third-party product is used instead of custom developed software, check if the product applies the proper mitigation and ensure a reasonable patch-level.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: SQL/NoSQL-Injection Prevention
mitigations.description: Try to use parameter binding to be safe from injection vulnerabilities. When a third-party product is used instead of custom developed software, check if the product applies the proper mitigation and ensure a reasonable patch-level.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Tool Server Authentication
mitigations.description: Authenticate every caller of the server, for example with OAuth 2.1 as the MCP specification describes for HTTP transports, and pass on the identity of the user an agent acts for, so that each tool call is authorized for that user. Expose the server only to the agents that need it.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Build Pipeline Hardening
mitigations.description: Apply DevSecOps best-practices and use scanning tools to identify vulnerabilities in source- or byte-code,dependencies, container layers, and optionally also via dynamic scans against running test systems.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Encryption of Technical Asset
mitigations.description: Apply encryption to the technical asset.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Encapsulation of Technical Asset
mitigations.description: Encapsulate the asset behind a guarding service, application, or reverse-proxy. For admin maintenance a bastion-host should be used as a jump-server. For file transfer a store-and-forward-host should be used as an indirect file exchange platform.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigations.name: Ingestion Integrity
mitigations.description: Ingest only content from vetted sources, record where each entry came from and validate it before it is embedded. Keep the entries of different users and tenants apart with access controls at retrieval time, limit what agents may write into their memory, and review and expire stored entries regularly.

attributes.threagile:check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?
